articles.title: Talking to yourself on psilocybin may be a good sign in alcohol treatment, small study hints
articles.summary: In a small psilocybin trial for alcohol use disorder, people who stayed alcohol-free three months later tended to describe an inner dialogue during their session, while those who returned to drinking talked more about sensations and visions.

articles.title: How the TikTok algorithm changed political campaigning in 2024
articles.summary: A new analysis of the 2024 U.S. presidential election reveals how TikTok’s design encourages candidates to use short, emotional, and performance-based videos. The study highlights how algorithmic platforms favor rapid entertainment and visual spectacle over detailed policy discussions.

articles.title: Sexual satisfaction is more closely tied to orgasm for women than for men, study finds
articles.summary: The orgasm gap shows up in Italy too: men reported more frequent orgasms than women. Among women, orgasm frequency was more closely tied to sexual satisfaction and oral sex, a new study finds.

articles.title: Male managers start hiring more women after their first daughter is born, study finds
articles.summary: Male managers who have a first daughter tend to hire more women and raise female employees' share of earnings, according to new research. The shift happens almost immediately and has no detectable impact on company performance.

articles.title: Brain receptors for dopamine and insulin coordinate to control compulsive eating
articles.summary: A new study reveals how dopamine and insulin receptors interact in the brain's emotional center to regulate compulsive eating. These findings offer biological clues to the strong link between food addiction and metabolic diseases like diabetes.

articles.title: Vagus Nerve Stimulation Could Help New Skills Stick
articles.summary: Stimulating the vagus nerve after practice helped mice develop stronger long-term motor learning, revealing a potentially important window when the brain is still locking in a new skill. The effect was linked to rhythmic changes in brain blood vessels, hinting that body-to-brain signals may help prepare the brain for lasting change.

articles.title: Two decades of U.S. data challenge an evolutionary explanation for the gender-equality paradox
articles.summary: Evolutionary psychologists have often argued that richer, more egalitarian societies amplify innate differences between men and women. However, two decades-long studies of Americans suggest otherwise, finding that rising wealth and gender equality do not widen the psychological divide.

articles.title: Do humans really have a ‘lizard brain’ lurking beneath our rational minds?
articles.summary: It’s a powerful analogy that captured the popular imagination, but the biological reality is quite different Humans have a cognitive quirk for the number three. Think of the many stories that use it, from The Three Little Pigs to Goldilocks and the Three Bears and The Three Musketeers. Public information and political campaigns use it for impact and ease of recall (“Stop, look and listen”; “See it. Say it. Sorted”…

articles.title: This diet may slow brain aging by 2.5 years
articles.summary: People who followed the MIND diet more closely showed slower brain shrinkage and less grey matter loss over time, with the strongest differences equivalent to about 2.5 years of delayed brain aging. Berries and poultry were linked with healthier brain changes, while sweets and fried fast foods were associated with greater tissue loss.

articles.title: Could quitting ultra-processed food boost your mental health?
articles.summary: People with depression who dramatically cut ultra-processed foods experienced notable improvements in their symptoms in a small preliminary study. Researchers suspect healthier eating may benefit the brain partly by reducing gut damage and chronic inflammation.

articles.title: Children at risk for depression get “stuck” on sad faces
articles.summary: Depression may change which emotional faces children notice most, but the pattern appears to depend on family history. Children at higher familial risk became increasingly focused on sad faces, while lower-risk children with rising symptoms paid less attention to happy ones.

articles.title: Brain scans reveal which disorders are linked to faster brain aging
articles.summary: A massive MRI study found that Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment, psychiatric disorders, and addiction are associated with distinct patterns of accelerated brain aging. The strongest effects appeared in Alzheimer’s and mild cognitive impairment, while ADHD and autism showed no significant overall difference.

articles.title: Brain responses to heartbeat are altered in patients with iRBD
articles.summary: Isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), a condition characterized by strong physical reactions to vivid, often violent dreams, is one of the earliest warning signs of brain changes seen in Parkinson's disease or dementia with Lewy bodies, sometimes appearing years before diagnosis.

articles.title: New imaging method links cells' spatial organization to cancer outcomes

articles.title: Your gut may be making a molecule that raises Alzheimer’s risk
articles.summary: Scientists have linked a gut bacterial compound called ImP to greater Alzheimer’s risk, harmful brain protein buildup, and faster cognitive decline. The finding raises the possibility that reducing ImP in the blood could one day help slow or prevent dementia.

articles.title: Vitamin C linked to fewer deaths in blood disorder trial
articles.summary: Vitamin C may do more than support the immune system. In a phase 2 trial of people with precancerous or low risk blood cancers, daily vitamin C did not slow abnormal cell growth, but it was linked to favorable changes in inflammation and fewer serious complications. An exploratory follow up also found fewer deaths among participants taking vitamin C than among those receiving placebo.
